issues.failure_explanation: The theorem quantifies M_i before the probability statement, i.e. as a deterministic constant. The proof obtains M_i from Gelfand's formula applied to L^{(i)}, which is built from W_i and hence from the random sketches S_i and \hat S; the M_i produced is therefore a random variable, and only the reversed statement (with probability 1-2δ there is a realization-dependent M_i) is proved. No uniformity of the Gelfand convergence over the good event is established.

issues.failure_explanation: W_i = I - μA^{-1}B with A, B symmetric positive definite is in general not symmetric, so it has no decomposition \tilde U_i Λ_i \tilde U_i^T with orthogonal \tilde U_i. The block-diagonalisation of L^{(i)} via P built from \tilde U_i therefore is not justified as written; one must use that A^{-1}B is similar to A^{-1/2}BA^{-1/2} (real eigenvalues, diagonalisable) and P^{-1} with \tilde U_i^{-1}.

Theorems lowerBoundai and a1 apply it for every a_i and conclude that a_i ≥ log_3[((1+ω)r+1)/ω] suffices for (14); Theorem cmpxtyAlgSLSE then sets a_i equal to these bounds, which are small constants (a_i < α ≈ 1–3). For such a_i the inequality is false in general: L^{(i)} contains an identity block so ‖L^{(i)}‖ ≥ 1 > 1/(3√2), and for a_i = 2 the block L_k^2 at λ = 19/36 has norm ≈ 0.7 ≫ 1/9. Hence the stated lower bounds do not guarantee (14).

issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Theorem lowerBoundai the quantity that bounds the ratio of successive sketched errors is r(i−1,i) = sqrt((m_i−d)/(m_{i−1}−d)) > 1 (the smaller sketch has larger error). With m_i = 2^{-(K+1-i)}N this equals sqrt((2−x_i)/(1−x_i)) ≥ √2, x_i = 2^{K+2−i}γ. The complexity proof instead uses its reciprocal sqrt((1−x_i)/(2−x_i)) < 1/√2, so the claimed bound a_i < α = log_3{[1+(1+ω)/√2]/ω} is false (the correct bound exceeds α and blows up as 2^Kγ → 1), the first-stage cost 4αNd is unsupported, and since sqrt((2−x)/(1−x)) increases in x while x_i decreases in i, the sequence a_i decreases, contradicting the asserted a_2 < … < a_K.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the correct r(i−1,i) = sqrt((2−x_i)/(1−x_i)); replace α by a γ,K-dependent constant α' = log_3{[1+(1+ω)sqrt((2−2^Kγ)/(1−2^Kγ))]/ω}, state a_2 > … > a_K, and correct the stated r in Theorem lowerBoundai.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constant α, the first-stage cost 4αNd, and the main-text monotonicity claim a_2<…<a_K (used to justify presenting only a_2 and a_K in Section 5.1) are wrong; the lower bound a_i > log_3(1/ω) and the second-stage bound remain valid.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma finalerror (and Theorem lowerBoundai via (26)) states finite-N inequalities with the explicit factor sqrt((N−d)/(m_i−d)). These come from Remark remarkA7, which converts the limit PE(i) → (1−γ)/(ξ−γ) of Lemma lemma:lemma3 (a statement about N → ∞ with fixed spectral-distribution and proportional-regime hypotheses) into a bound on the finite-N ratio, and then passes from second moments to first moments only under an unverified variance hypothesis that appears in no theorem statement. Neither step is justified for the finite N, d, m_i to which Lemma finalerror and Theorem lowerBoundai apply; Theorem lowerBoundai additionally needs a lower bound on E‖X(\tildeβ^i−β)‖ that the remark never provides. Moreover the regime d/N → γ > 0 required by Lemma lemma:lemma3 and adopted in Theorem cmpxtyAlgSLSE is incompatible with the embedding hypothesis m_1 > r ≥ cε^{-2}(d+log(N/δ))log(ed/δ) that underlies the 1/3 rate: with d = γN and m_1 = 2^{-K}N the requirement forces 2^{-K}/γ > cε^{-2}log(ed/δ) → ∞.
